we have derived a closed-form expression to quantify the residual self-interference for OFDM systems in presence of both phase noise and I/Q imbalance.

the effects of phase noise and I/Q imbalance can be approximately decouple for small phase noise and I-Q imbalance levels and the average self-interference is linearly proportional the I-Q image rejection ratio and the phase noise 3dB bandwidth.

the residual SI analysis for full-duplex transceivers under PN and IQI.
the analysis of residual self-interference in full-duplex systems.

the residual SI power is a function of the channel taps’ powers, PN 3-db bandwidth, and IQ image rejection ratio.
the effects of IQI and PN can be approximately decouple for small PN and low IQI levels.

the effects of phase noise and I/Q imbalance can be decoupled for a full-duplex transceiver with perfect cancellation, and this decoupling is more effective when the phase noise is small and the I/Q imbalance is low.

PN and IQI are two key impairments that should be considered in the analysis of full-duplex transceivers.

, in full-duplex systems with perfect digital-domain SI cancellation, the average residual SI can be significantly reduced by employing low-power IQI and PN.
the effects of the RF impairments on the residual SI can be decoupled for a small level of impairments, which can be useful in designing full-duplex transceivers.
